   - `risk_of_bias_tool`: Pick the single design-matched tool per `RISK_OF_BIAS.md` §1:
     * `"RoB 2 (parallel-trial variant)"` (individually randomized trial)
     * `"RoB 2 (cluster-randomized trials variant)"` (cluster-randomized trial — check unit of randomization carefully!)
     * `"ROBINS-I"` (non-randomized intervention / quasi-experimental study with a genuine comparator: DiD, IV, RDD, PSM, ITS, controlled before-after, policy panel FE)
     * `"JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross Sectional Studies"` (quantitative cross-sectional survey / observational regression without quasi-experimental intervention comparator)
     * `"JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Cohort Studies"` (observational longitudinal cohort study without intervention framing)
     * `"CASP Qualitative Checklist"` (primary qualitative study: interviews, focus groups, ethnography, qualitative case study)
     * `"MMAT (Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool)"` (genuine mixed-methods study combining both qualitative and quantitative primary components)
     * `"AMSTAR 2"` (systematic review, meta-analysis, or scoping review with systematic search/screening; NEVER use for non-systematic narrative literature reviews)
     * `"Legal Institutional Evidence Appraisal Framework"` (legal-empirical, doctrinal-empirical, jurimetric, or institutional-historical study that fits none of the six conventional designs above)
     * `"NONE"` (fits none of the listed tools, e.g., pure mathematical/simulation optimization model, or non-systematic narrative review/essay without primary empirical data or systematic search — explain why in `comment`)
   - `mechanism_certainty`: Single integer `"0"`, `"1"`, `"2"`, `"3"`, or `"4"` strictly obeying `CODEBOOK.md` §9 and its design ceiling:

     * `"3"` ONLY for `RoB 2` trials OR `ROBINS-I` studies with credible Low/Moderate overall risk of bias

(`"2"` = mechanism directly observed empirically; `"1"` = documented statistical/descriptive association; `"0"` = inferred only by authors).

country.comment: Primary empirical focus is urban drinking water systems in Ethiopia across four case-study cities (Addis Ababa, Adama, Mekelle and Dire Dawa), situated alongside secondary WHO/JMP comparisons across Sub-Saharan Africa.
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Title & Abstract; PDF pp. 6-8, Section 3.1

effect_estimate.comment: Qualitative findings from key informant interviews and field visits identify weak legal and institutional security, regional bureau control over local water enterprises' project structure and financing, weak multilevel coordination, informal urban expansion beyond distribution pressure zones, lack of citizen participation, inconvenient in-office bill settlement and sparse branch offices, and unenforced Western-modeled water pollution laws as key barriers to sustainable service. Quantitative simulations also estimate that installing pressure-reducing valves cuts high-pressure nodes (>50 m) from 33% to 8% in Addis Ababa and from 38% to 9% in Dire Dawa, while integrated water management scenarios reduce 2050 unmet water demand by 65%, 87%, 66% and 67% across Addis Ababa, Adama, Mekelle and Dire Dawa, respectively.
effect_estimate.value: Qualitative for legal/institutional mechanisms — no numeric effect estimate reported linking governance variables to access; quantitatively, 2021 urban water supply coverage was 66.11% in Addis Ababa (deficit 235.83 MLD), 78.94% in Adama (deficit 9.13 MLD), 51.58% in Mekelle (deficit 25.81 MLD) and 94.43% in Dire Dawa (deficit 2.32 MLD), with 0% 24/7 continuous piped supply and non-revenue water losses of 38.49%, 36.01%, 35.19% and 42.79%, respectively
effect_estimate.where_found: Table 2, PDF p. 12; Table 3, PDF p. 14; Section 4.1.8, PDF pp. 20-21; Table 5, PDF p. 24; Section 5, PDF pp. 27-28

mechanism_certainty.comment: Field visits and key informant interviews directly document administrative and institutional mechanisms affecting urban water delivery (e.g., municipal enterprise delivery mandate vs regional water bureau control over technical structure and financing in Adama, informal horizontal expansion exceeding WDN pressure zones, inconvenient in-office bill-settlement procedures and few branch offices, lack of citizen participation and non-enforcement of imported water pollution policies). Capped at 2 by the mixed-methods design ceiling.
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF pp. 20-21, Section 4.1.8; PDF p. 25, Section 4.2.4
